column1: # --- minilang literals: delimiters, escapes, and the open form ------------
# `+name<delim>src<delim>`. An unescaped delimiter closes it; unescaped

column1: # `/f` `/s` `/N` `/q` `/r` `/u` `/t` stack in any order, with f/s mutually
# exclusive and q exclusive with both r and u. An out-of-int64 digit run and
# a repeated letter are REJECTED, while a non-modifier tail (`/1x`) leaves
# the whole text as one word — three different outcomes that are easy to
# collapse into one. On a paren group the same suffix becomes a leading
# sugar value instead. NUR059: canon spells `a/u` and `a/2` as a bare
# `word(a)`, dropping the modifier — both engines agree, so these rows pin
# the shared render and a one-sided fix fails loudly.
# --- optional keys, shorthand entries, and modifiers on keys --------------
# `a?:` desugars to a disjunct with None and Absent. The shorthand forms
# (`{a/r}`, `{a/t}`) take the base name as the key and keep the FULL token
# as the value, so the modifier qualifies the value; spelling one on the
# key itself (`{a/r: 1}`) is illegal_key. `{a/}` has no valid modifier at
# all, so the slash stays part of both key and value.
